- When sentiment is positive (≥0.4) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) or neutral, model often underestimates; adjust downward by 3–7% to align with mean reversion.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., >85.0) — cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-period moving average to smooth.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: true prices often dip 1–3 days after model peak — shift forecast down 1–2 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows rising optimism (e.g., 0.0 → 0.67 → 1.00), model overreacts; apply downward correction of 5–8% to prevent overbought bias.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon — if forecast is >10% above 18-day moving average, reduce by 2–5% unless sentiment is strong bullish.
